newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rises on deferreds, May flat by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rises on deferreds, May flat by close.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE coffee futures shaved gains by the close on Thursday but deferred months posted double-digit advances on back of light volume.
Traders said roaster price-fixing at the lower levels provided an immediate floor. There was little origin selling pressure with Indonesian offers, suprisingly, falling to a trickle.
"Surprisingly, there are no fresh offers from Indonesia of late," said one. Indonesia, the world's top robusta producer, has begun to harvest and ship its main crop.
Benchmark May wiped early gains to end the day unchanged at $1,580, the session's low, after filling the upside chart gap at $1,590 and $1,610.
July posted a $2 gain to finish at $1,585, with the active May/July spread finishing at $5 over against level money on Wednesday.
Traders said the nearby structure has tightened after the funds had more or less rolled the spot May positions far forward.
Volume stood at 4,137 lots, dominated by May and July contracts.
All eyes focussed on volatile New York arabica coffee futures which saw prices falling back slightly on Thursday after posting a seven percent rise on Wednesday.

But traders said the movements were technically-induced. The fundamental picture remained unchanged with the immediate availabilities were fairly good following heavy sales by origins at the height of market rally earlier in the year.
Technically, London's May faces further resistance at this month's reaction high of $1,668. The further upside target is $1,675. On the downside, support is seen at $1,570.
Commenting on New York's move overnight, broker GNI said: "Activity was however far from booming, but the rally tends to make the charts look a little more positive."

In other news, Colombian exporters have begun rushing to get shipments to port ahead of a strike by truck drivers set for April 20, industry sources said. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
